title: League of Legends Patch 26.15 Notes
overview: Patch 26.15 opens Season 3 with a full Bel'Veth rework that trades her early-invade power for an infinitely scaling ultimate, nerfs to the patch's overperformers (Locke, Naafiri, Riven, Sylas, Mordekaiser), and tank/marksman buffs. Ranked is retuned to reward winning outright, and the permanent League Classic mode launches.
summary: Bel'Veth is now a late-game monster: worse early stats and a slow Q, but a permanent True Form at 80 stacks.
Locke, Naafiri, Riven, Sylas, and Mordekaiser all got taken down a peg — your carry games just got harder.
Alistar, Maokai, Volibear, and Zac got buffs, so the frontline is punching back.
Ranked Season 3 removes loss protection entirely — Aegis of Valor only pays out on wins now.
changelogHighlights: League Classic launched — a permanent mode with 60 champions on their classic kits and old items like Heart of Gold.
Arena adds the Ok Boomerang augment and removes Slow and Steady, with several augments capped at level 2.

champions.summary: Reworked from early-game invader into a late-game scaling evolution threat.
champions.details: Her base attack speed (0.85 to 0.67), AD (60 to 55), health (610 to 580), and armor (32 to 28) all dropped and Q - Void Surge now has a 4s cooldown at rank 1 instead of 1s, but W, E, and her R passive application all scale far harder and Endless Banquet's buff becomes permanent at 80 stacks — meaning early ganks and invades will feel awful, and every game you play is now a race to stack up and never leave True Form.
champions.name: Bel'Veth

champions.summary: Health, Q damage, and W move speed all cut.
champions.details: Base health drops 655 to 620, Q damage is reduced, and W's move speed is now capped at 40% with less grey health, so the free lane bullying and disengage that carried Locke players is gone and you'll actually have to respect trades.
champions.name: Locke

champions.summary: Ultimate damage and per-packmate scaling reduced.
champions.details: R damage falls from 150/225/300 to 125/200/275 with weaker per-packmate scaling, so those one-shot ultimate dives on squishies now leave them alive — expect to need a follow-up instead of a solo execute.
champions.name: Naafiri

champions.summary: Ultimate AD ratio and Wind Slash scaling lowered.
champions.details: R's AD ratio drops from 25% to 20% and Wind Slash's ratio is also reduced, so your full combo no longer converts a healthy target into a kill and Riven's burst-through-armor windows get noticeably shorter.
champions.name: Riven

champions.summary: Q's first lash damage reduced at higher ranks.
champions.details: First-lash damage goes from 40/65/90/115/140 to 40/60/80/100/120, weakening Sylas's poke-based lane pressure and making his all-in more dependent on landing the stolen ultimate.
champions.name: Sylas

champions.summary: R steals fewer stats, with an E cooldown buff as consolation.
champions.details: Death Realm now steals 10% of stats instead of 13% (plus a bug fix), so winning the 1v1 you dragged someone into is less automatic — though a lower E cooldown gives you more chances to set it up.
champions.name: Mordekaiser

champions.summary: Passive damage and per-stack scaling increased.
champions.details: Plasma now deals 4-30 damage scaling with AP and +1-8 per stack, giving Kai'Sa noticeably better mid-game trading and a stronger reason to build AP items into her evolutions.
champions.name: Kai'Sa

champions.summary: Q monster damage and AP ratio up.
champions.details: Q gains a +10% monster modifier and its AP ratio rises from 40% to 50%, making jungle Maokai clear faster and hit harder with AP builds instead of pure tank stats.
champions.name: Maokai

champions.summary: Armor growth and E cooldown improved.
champions.details: Armor growth goes 4.7 to 5.2 with a lower E cooldown, so Zac holds up better into scaling ADCs and can throw himself into fights more often.
champions.name: Zac

champions.summary: Q cooldown reduced at all ranks.
champions.details: A lower Q cooldown across every rank means more frequent stun-chases in lane and jungle, tightening Volibear's gank and skirmish windows.
champions.name: Volibear

champions.details: Move speed rises from 330 to 335, a small but real help for landing the W-Q flip that every Alistar game hinges on.
champions.name: Alistar

items.summary: Cheaper and Shaped Charge hits harder.
items.details: Cost drops 3200g to 3000g and Shaped Charge now deals 50 + 150% lethality, making it a much stronger and earlier first item for lethality bruisers and assassins.
items.name: Bastionbreaker

items.summary: Cost cut to 750g with 45% attack speed.
items.details: At 750g for 45% attack speed it becomes an extremely efficient early crit component, so marksmen can rush it without falling behind on tempo.
items.name: Yun Tal Wildarrows

items.summary: Shadow effect now scales with AD and AP.
items.details: Shadow gives 30 plus 10% bonus AD and 10% AP, meaning the item keeps growing in the late game instead of falling off as your other items come online.
items.name: Terminus

systems.summary: League Classic launches as a permanent mode.
systems.details: 60 champions play with classic versions of their kits alongside old items like Heart of Gold, emphasizing strategy and stronger consequences over mechanics — a whole separate skill test from Summoner's Rift.

systems.summary: Season 3 removes loss protection and reworks Aegis of Valor.
systems.details: Aegis of Valor no longer reduces LP loss on defeat and instead awards double LP on wins with no minimum mastery score, so padding your KDA in a loss earns you nothing — only wins move your rank.

systems.summary: Duo queue returns to Master with restrictions.
systems.details: Master players can duo with someone close in rank, while Grandmaster, Challenger, and anyone with GM/Challenger MMR cannot duo at all — so high-elo players lose their premade safety net.

systems.summary: Augment pool reshuffled with new, removed, and capped augments.
systems.details: Ok Boomerang is added (level 2 fires a second boomerang), Slow and Steady is removed, Demonic Clasp, Critical Rhythm, Laser Eyes, Spellwake, Earthwake, and Tap Dancer cap at level 2, HiveMind and Ominous Pact are buffed, and crit-to-adaptive-force conversion improves from 0.68:1 to 1:1 — crit builds are meaningfully better and prismatic-stacking strategies are reined in.

systems.summary: Mayhem damage modifiers now apply to spells, items, and augments.
systems.details: Per-champion damage modifiers extend beyond abilities to items and augments, plus augment buffs to Warding Weapon, Squishy Slappy Grab, and Titan's Resolve and a Critical Missile damage cut — balance outliers in Mayhem should feel far less extreme.

systems.summary: Jack of All Trades gives less adaptive force.
systems.details: Breakpoint adaptive force drops from 10/25 to 8/20, so the stat-stacking builds that abuse many cheap components lose some of their free damage.
